Choose a mock mode. A short description of the selection appears below. See the user guide (Geoposition) for details.

In enhancement modes: where heading change for path dead-reckoning comes from. Gyroscope — HU sensor; steering — steering-wheel angle from the bus (needs zero and scale calibration); gyro+steer — gyro primary, steer confirms turns, fills in when gyro is quiet or stale, and while moving pulls toward steer when it leads on the same side (not a sum; a held wheel does not rotate a stopped car).
Steering angle is unavailable right now — gyroscope is used until a signal appears.
Steering angle is unavailable right now — heading uses gyroscope only until steer returns.
Navigation gets satellite data as-is. No car speed override and no path extrapolation when the signal is lost.
While satellites are good: position and course from GPS, speed from the car (smoother). If the signal is lost — hold the last point and extrapolate with sensors (up to 10 minutes).
Enhance mock only when geoposition is lost
While satellites are good — normal GPS. If the signal is lost — hold the last point and extrapolate with car speed and gyro (up to 10 minutes).

Continuous shadow position from car speed and gyro; satellites are soft-blended by quality. If the shadow drifts far from trusted GNSS, it is re-snapped. No 10-minute cutoff. When the junk filter is on, bad GNSS is not blended and not stored as last-good. Optional background auto-calibration on large mismatch.

Advanced mode only. On a sustained shadow↔GNSS mismatch, quietly calibrates on-road speed and heading: gyro yaw L/R, and when heading uses the wheel also the steer scale profile (zero, deadzone, and wheelbase stay as-is). Idle gyro zero is a separate toggle. Off by default.
All enhancement modes (not Direct). With good GNSS, refines left/right turn scale on arcs; saved to disk. Requires heading source Gyroscope. Off by default.
Advanced mode only. While parked, quietly calibrates yaw bias and records temperature (warm-up drift). Off by default.
In enhancement modes (not Direct), invert travel course while reversing. Source: HU PRND, else reverse switch, else TBox. On by default.
Softly pulls the DR shadow toward OSM roads (not every tick). Needs a downloaded region with coverage. Off by default. Available in enhancement modes and «No fix».
Current behaviour: soft pull to the road, leash, and free particle.
Shadow stays on the road graph; gyro/steer pick forks. Large gap or courtyard breaks onto the free particle. Default: Ordinary.
Experiment: Ordinary snap, but heading pulls harder toward the selected (blue) road. Fully unsnaps 30 m before a junction of more than 2 lines (any fork or exit); snaps again 10 m after it.

On-road calibration: drive forward with good GNSS at varying speeds (several ~10 km/h bands, steady windows only) and smooth long turns (≥4 fitted arcs left and ≥4 right, ≥30°). Turn progress counts successful fits, not coarse segments. Gyro gets yaw scale/sign; CAN→GNSS speed scale is shared. Steering zero/scale are unchanged. Reverse gear / bad fix / no CAN·gyro / course jumps pause collection. Enough or auto-fill → preview → Save.

Steering heading uses manual zero, sign, deadzone, vehicle wheelbase, and scale knots at 20/40/60/80 km/h (defaults 0.072 / 0.072 / 0.042 / 0.033; sign 1, zero 0°). Scale is linearly interpolated between knots and held at the nearest endpoint outside them. On-road calibration fits the tan model from ≥5 fitted arcs left and right, ≥30°, with at least 2 arcs in three speed bands. Shared CAN→GNSS speed scale is fitted separately.

Uses wheel rotation and auto-tunes against the dashboard odometer. Below 70%% reliability it is not used. After calibration you can enable it for trips and for path extrapolation.

Only calm kilometres count: no sharp turns, no reverse, and no hard accel or braking (speed swing over a kilometre above 40 km/h).
